In this story, a young couple, Jim and Della, sacrifice their most prized possessions to buy each other Christmas gifts, only to find that their sacrifices render the gifts useless. Jim sells his watch to buy Della a set of combs for her beautiful hair, while Della cuts her hair to buy Jim a chain for his watch. The irony lies in their love and sacrifice, which ultimately leads to an unforeseen twist where both gifts become futile, revealing the depth of their affection, yet underscoring the bittersweetness of their situation. Another notable instance of irony exists in the realm of politics, epitomized by George Orwell’s "Animal Farm." Here, the pigs, who lead the revolution against human tyranny, gradually become indistinguishable from the oppressive humans they overthrew. This transformation illustrates situational irony, where the intended outcome of freedom and equality devolves into a new form of oppression. Lastly, consider the classic example of a fire station burning down; you'd expect the one place equipped to handle fires to be safe from them, but the reality defies that expectation, making it a stark reminder of how life often plays out in unexpected ways. These examples underscore how irony can serve as a powerful tool

Question: What is it about women that confuses men so much?
Old_Answer: She comes home late. You both are in a live-in relationship. 'You know, today my boss did the same thing. He gave me the tough tasks and assigned Ritika the easy ones as he's somewhat into her.’ You nod. She continues. 'I'm planning to change my project. I even talked to my HR and the HR said…' You stop her in between. 'I know what the HR said. I've been listening to this story for a week now. Please change the company as that's the only option.’ you say. 'But this company has all the perks I ever wished for. And it's just been four months. It's not about the company, it's about that one person.’ she replies. ‘If you know what the problem is, then why don't you take strict action against it?’ he asks. 'I'm trying, trust me. I was telling you what happened today but you stopped me in between.’ she says. 'Oh, great. So now you'll point things at me. As always.’ he smirks. And they picked up a fight. Women and men are poles apart when it comes to dealing with problems. Women like to talk. They want to vent things out when they are in trouble. And when they do, they don't do it to get preached. They 'just’ want to vent out. Men are problem solvers. The very moment they listen to a problem, they can't help and start giving advice. They can't listen like a wall. And that's where the conflict takes place. Men talk about their problems once in a blue moon. When they are overwhelmed, they just hide inside a tunnel. They hide themselves and don't speak about it. And when someone talks about their problems, men think the other person really needs some advice. Nope. It doesn't work that way with women. Just be a calm listener. Be patient. Nod. Pat her. Caress her. Because that's what she expects when she is talking to her favourite person. That. Not any advice. Unless they are asking for it, of course. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Then she started developing a crush on me and the bhaiya word started vanishing. I got it. My friends started forcing me to propose to her. I wrote a long letter. I was reading it out on the call when she said ‘I love you’. Our conversation started going ‘there’ eventually. You see? From bhaiya to having those conversations. It's ridiculous. If you're a girl, you can date only the guys of your age because the older ones, you call them bhaiya. The younger ones, your parents won't allow you to get married to them. If you're a guy, you can never date a senior. You call her didi. And if the girl you like is younger than you, and she calls you bhaiya, then it's game over. You can only date girls of your age. What a shame, right? These setups were made centuries back. Now we're living in the age of love marriages. The only suggestion I can give you is, don't kill your chances.
